pinned_formal_rules.name: checkMultiplicityRangeExpressionTypeFeaturing
pinned_formal_rules.description: The bounds of a MultiplicityRange must have the same featuringTypes as the MultiplicityRange.

pinned_formal_rules.name: checkMultiplicityTypeFeaturing
pinned_formal_rules.description: If the owningType of a Multiplicity is a Feature, then the Multiplicity must have the same featuringTypes as that Feature. Otherwise, it must have no featuringTypes (meaning that it is implicitly featured by the base Classifier Anything).
pinned_formal_rules.ocl: if owningType <> null and owningType.oclIsKindOf(Feature) then     featuringType =          owningType.oclAsType(Feature).featuringType else     featuringType->isEmpty() endif

current_issues.current_text_summary: Multiplicity ownership does not use FeatureMembership, so owningType is null. The issue proposes owningNamespace in both the description and OCL.
A cross Feature has the opposite end or Cartesian domain. Its multiplicity bound must instead resolve names in the containing Association or Connector through the owning end Feature domain.

FeatureAdapter.java.behavior: The owningNamespace, when a Feature, supplies implicit featuring types.

ExpressionAdapter.java.behavior: MultiplicityRange bounds on an owned cross Feature receive the owning end Feature featuring types. The v9 interpretation applies this same domain consistently to the MultiplicityRange and its bound Expressions.
